paras: The lynching of Peter Corbin was the reported killing of a prisoner taken from the Gilmer county jail at Ellijay, Georgia, by a party of masked men in early 1882. Corbin, charged with an outrage on a lady, was reported found the next day in woods near the town with his head severed from his body. The only account is a short item from the Dalton Citizen, which passed the story on as something it had learned and hoped was untrue.

According to the Dalton Citizen, Corbin was charged with committing an outrage on a lady in Gilmer county. Deputy Marshal King arrested him "in this place", the town where the Citizen was published, "week before last" and turned him over to the sheriff of Gilmer county. Neither copy of the item gives Corbin's race or names the woman.

The sheriff took Corbin back to Ellijay and placed him in the county jail. The night after the sheriff's return, "a party of masked men" took him from the jail. He was found the next day "in a piece of woods near the town with his head completely severed from his body." The item gives no date for the killing, no number for the masked party, and no description of how Corbin died beyond the condition of the body.
No report of an inquest, arrests or a grand jury inquiry appears in the coverage found.

The story reached print through Georgia papers' columns of state news, which reprinted the Dalton Citizen's paragraph among unrelated items. The earliest copy found ran in the Savannah Morning News on 18 March 1882, credited to the Citizen and ending with the description of the body. The Marietta Journal printed the fuller version on 23 March, including the Citizen's comment: "We are opposed to lynch law under any circumstances, and hope the story is not true." Neither paper added comment of its own or ran a follow-up confirming or denying the report.

bases: Both copies of the Dalton Citizen item report that a party of masked men took Corbin, charged with an outrage, from the Gilmer county jail and that he was found dead in the woods next day [A1, A2].

The Dalton Citizen reported that masked men took Corbin, a prisoner charged with an outrage on a lady, from jail and that he was found beheaded in the woods [A1, A2]; the size of the 'party' is not given, and the Citizen itself passed the story on as hearsay ('We learn') and hoped it was not true [A2].
Both texts found are reprints of the same Dalton Citizen item [A1, A2]; no independent report, local Gilmer county account or follow-up was found.
